policy_title: Establish an Ethics and Integrity Commission and Reform Ministerial Conduct
stated: Labour will establish a new independent Ethics and Integrity Commission with its own Chair to ensure probity in government. They will review and update post-government employment rules to end abuses, enforcing restrictions on ministers lobbying former regulators with meaningful sanctions. The Independent Adviser on Ministerial Interests will be given powers to initiate investigations and access evidence.

source.quote: Labour will restore confidence in government and ensure ministers are held to the highest standards. We will establish a new independent Ethics and Integrity Commission, with its own independent Chair, to ensure probity in government. Labour will review and update post-government employment rules to end flagrant abuses seen under the Conservatives. This includes enforcing restrictions on ministers lobbying for the companies they used to regulate, with meaningful sanctions for breaching the rules. We will give the Independent Adviser on Ministerial Interests the powers to start investigations into misconduct and ensure they have access to the evidence they need.

bearing_set.reason: An independent Ethics and Integrity Commission with enforcement powers over ministerial conduct directly advances rule of law, due process in public office, and democratic accountability — core O9 indicators.

Credible government ethics enforcement is a measurable driver of institutional trust; reduced scandal and stronger probity rules plausibly improve public trust in democratic institutions, a component of social trust surveys (e.g. British Social Attitudes, Edelman).

membership_note: The policy is squarely in the governance-integrity and democratic-accountability space. O9 is the primary bearing (rule of law, due process). O15 earns a real verdict because institutional trust — not just political satisfaction — is a measured indicator of social trust and cohesion. Other fundamentals (O10 for revolving-door employment restrictions, O12 for commission running costs) do not clear the non-negligible bar: post-employment lobbying bans are professional conduct rules on those exercising public power rather than personal liberty coercion in the O10 sense, and the fiscal cost is trivially small.
